_comment: Allocation exact-pin baseline (round-21 T8, maintainer-ruled rider from
Issues/round22/RESEARCH-97-PERCENT-GATES.md, allocation-gate row). Gate:
scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -BenchSmoke (part of -Nightly) re-runs the benchmark suite in smoke mode
(DWARF_BENCH_SMOKE=1, ShortRun) and FAILS unless every pinned scenario's MemoryDiagnoser
BytesAllocatedPerOperation EQUALS its pin exactly. Allocated bytes per op are deterministic for a
fixed SDK - verified 2026-08-21 by two full smoke runs on this machine: all 41 benchmarks were
byte-identical across runs, so 'unstable' is empty and every DwarfMapper scenario is pinned.
UPDATE PROTOCOL (the measured-floor philosophy applied to allocations): an UNEXPLAINED increase is
a regression; an unexplained DECREASE is also a finding - the gate reports and fails on BOTH
directions. The only fix is a deliberate commit that re-measures (run the smoke, read the new
numbers) and updates this file WITH THE REASON in the same commit. The measuring commit for the
current pins is therefore always `git log -1 -- <this file>`. An SDK change is the one legitimate
silent-change vector, so the gate also compares the running SDK against measuredWith.sdk and
demands the same re-measure-and-update-together move.
Timing numbers from a smoke run are NON-GATES (see SmokeConfig in Program.cs). Only DwarfMapper's
OWN scenarios (*_Dwarf) are pinned; competitor rows (Mapperly/Mapster/AutoMapper) and Flat_Hand are
informational context printed by the gate, never gated.
totalBenchmarks pins the executed-benchmark COUNT: BenchmarkRunner exits 0 even when individual
benchmarks crash (they become NA rows), and a stray --filter would silently shrink the suite - the
count plus the per-row Statistics/Memory presence check is what makes 'every benchmark still runs'
mechanical rather than hoped.

2026-08-23 (round 25 T4): four BlitRatio_* scenarios added, 41 -> 45 benchmarks. They are the two blit-vs-scalar-twin pairs the ratio gate reads. Their allocation pins are recorded here like any other DwarfMapper scenario, but note what the ~4 KB gap between each Fast and Scalar arm is and is NOT: the Scalar arm's element type is [StructLayout(Auto)], which the runtime pads from 12 to 16 bytes, so the gap measures PADDING, not the copy strategy. That is precisely why the ratio gate reads TIMES rather than bytes for this comparison - allocations would look like a difference while measuring the wrong thing.

2026-08-23 (round 26): four NumList_* scenarios added, 45 -> 49 benchmarks. int[] -> List<long>, the shape where the value-element span fill can show through — the existing List category uses REFERENCE elements, where allocating the destination objects dominates and the fill strategy is invisible. Only NumList_Dwarf is pinned; the three competitor rows are informational like every other competitor row. Note the pin EQUALS Mapperly's and Mapster's 8,112 B: the win here is fill efficiency, not allocation, which is exactly why it needed a timing comparison rather than the allocation gate to surface.

2026-08-26 (round 27): the enum category was reworked to compare LIKE FOR LIKE, 53 -> 55 benchmarks. It previously pitted DwarfMapper's by-NAME mapping against competitors doing by-VALUE, which measures two different operations and flatters whichever one is cheaper. Now there are two categories: Enum_* is by-name (Dwarf, Mapperly configured with EnumMappingStrategy.ByName, AutoMapper) and EnumByValue_* is by-value (Dwarf opted in via [DwarfMapper(EnumStrategy = ByValue)], Mapperly and Mapster at their defaults). Net +2 rather than +3: Enum_Mapster moved into the by-value category rather than being duplicated, because Mapster has no by-name mode to configure. EnumByValue_Dwarf is pinned at 24 B/op, the same as its by-name twin - the strategy changes which comparison is fair, not what is allocated.

2026-08-23 (round 26, second addition): four NestedFill_* scenarios, 49 -> 53 benchmarks. A realistic graph mixing BOTH fill strategies in one map — reference-element Lines on the Add path, value-element Totals and per-line Quantities on the span fill. NumList isolates the fill strategy; this measures what is left of it beside the cost of allocating nested destination objects. Only the Dwarf row is pinned.

2026-09-03 (round 29, T0.2): two SpanBlit_* scenarios added, 55 -> 57 benchmarks. SpanBlit_Dwarf is the zero-alloc span map void Map(ReadOnlySpan<Vec3Src> src, Span<Vec3Dst> dst) taking the BlittableProof block copy (MemoryMarshal.Cast + CopyTo) into a preallocated destination array; SpanBlit_Scalar is its [StructLayout(Auto)] twin (Vec3Ren), which keeps the per-element loop — same pair-selection discipline as BlitRatio. Both pin at 0 B/op: every element is a value-type struct copied into a preallocated destination array, so neither path allocates anything, unlike the array/list blit rows above which allocate the destination array itself.

2026-09-07 (round 29, Phase 1): two View_* scenarios added, 57 -> 59 benchmarks. They are a PAIR and the pair is the measurement: both read the same six members of the same 1,000 VwOrder graphs into the same preallocated sink, and differ only in whether a VwOrderDto was built first. View_Dwarf pins at 0 B/op, which is the feature rather than a detail of it - a view that allocated anything would not be a view - and View_Map_Dwarf pins at 48,000 B, one 48-byte DTO per element. Read the TIME ratio with its population attached: 2.82 us against 6.04 us is 0.47x here, NOT the 0.20x / 0.04x of Issues/round29/plan3-results.md, because that probe's baseline built a FOUR-OBJECT destination graph per element while this one builds a single flat DTO. Same feature, a fairer and much less flattering baseline. What neither number claims is that a view is always free: a converter a view calls allocates on its own account, once per READ rather than once per map, so a view read many times can cost more than one Map. This pair has no converter, which is what makes it a clean measurement of the view itself.
